reasons: Types only, with no tests or runtime checks visible.

terms.meaning: a written description of the shape an object must have
a company or service that supplies AI models
a setting for how varied the AI's answers are; lower is steadier

sections.name: ChatMessage
sections.title: A single chat message
sections.what: One message in a conversation, with the speaker (system, user or assistant) and the text.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the common chat format that AI services accept.
sections.watch_out: Only three roles are allowed, so any other role name will fail type checks.

sections.name: ModelResponse
sections.title: Shape of a model's reply
sections.what: What a model call returns: the text, which model and provider answered, and optional token counts.
sections.why: Likely reason: records which model answered and how many tokens it used.
sections.watch_out: Token counts are optional, so code reading them must handle their absence.

sections.name: ModelProvider
sections.title: Contract every provider must follow
sections.what: Describes what a provider must offer: a name, a check that it is configured, and a chat call that returns a reply. The OpenAI and OpenRouter adapters both follow it.
sections.why: Lets the router use any provider in the same way.
sections.watch_out: A new provider must implement all three parts or it will not type-check.

sections.name: ChatOptions
sections.title: Options for a model call
sections.what: Optional settings for one call: randomness (temperature), maximum reply length, and whether the reply must be JSON.
sections.why: Lets callers tune each request without changing the provider.
sections.watch_out: The JSON setting asks the provider for JSON, but nothing here checks that the reply parses.

sections.name: ModelRouterConfig
sections.title: Three model slots
sections.what: Holds the names of the primary, fallback and cheap models that the router uses.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though the router comments say all three currently point to one model.
sections.watch_out: All three are normally set to the same model, so the fallback and cheap slots give no real protection.

summary: Defines the shared shapes for chat messages, model replies, model providers and router settings.
purpose: Gives all model code one agreed format, so providers can be swapped without rewriting callers.
why: Likely reason: to keep the OpenAI and OpenRouter adapters interchangeable behind one contract.
how: 1. Defines a chat message with a role and text. 2. Defines a reply with text, model name, provider name and optional token counts. 3. Defines what each provider must offer: a name, an availability check and a chat call. 4. Defines call options such as randomness, length limit and JSON output. 5. Defines three model slots: primary, fallback and cheap.
inputs: None at run time. These are compile-time shapes only.
risks: Types are removed when the code runs, so bad data from a provider is not caught here.
debug: If a compile error names one of these shapes, check the provider or caller that passes the data. Check that token counts are present before reading them.
